flashcard_questions.a: A circuit where components are connected end-to-end in a single loop, giving current only one path.
A circuit where components sit on separate branches, giving the current more than one path.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the current compare at different points in a series circuit?
flashcard_questions.a: It is the same everywhere: Itotal = I1 = I2 = I3

flashcard_questions.q: How do the voltages across components in a series circuit relate to the supply?
flashcard_questions.a: They add up to the supply voltage: Vtotal = V1 + V2 + V3

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the total resistance of resistors joined in series?
How does the total current from the supply relate to the branch currents in parallel?
What is the potential difference across each branch of a parallel circuit?
flashcard_questions.a: It equals the supply voltage: Vtotal = V1 = V2 = V3

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the total resistance of two resistors joined in parallel?
Resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 10 Ω are joined in series. What is the total resistance?
Resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are joined in parallel. What is the total resistance?
How does the total resistance of a parallel combination compare with its smallest resistor?
flashcard_questions.a: It is always smaller than the smallest individual resistor.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the total resistance when another resistor is added in parallel?
flashcard_questions.a: It falls, because the extra branch gives current another path to flow along.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the rest of a series circuit when one component breaks?
flashcard_questions.a: The whole circuit stops working, because the single loop is broken.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the other branches of a parallel circuit when one component breaks?
flashcard_questions.a: They carry on working, because each branch still has its own path to the cell.

flashcard_questions.q: Why are household appliances wired in parallel rather than in series?
flashcard_questions.a: So every device gets the full 230 V mains supply, whatever else is switched on.
